compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Running `rebar review-plan` on epic `759e-7dc1-675c-4877` (compliant-lemon-grunion, an epic with no `file_impact`, so it falls to the `CURRENCY_BASIS_FAIL_SAFE` / unscoped-whole-HEAD path in `attest.py:648-663`) produces a PASS verdict, but signing then fails with `stale-head`: the "current HEAD" reported does not match the code repo's real state.

Concretely: `rebar ls-remote origin main` and `rebar ls-remote gerrit main` both confirm the real, current `main` tip is `4dafd36d2aa1f0e264634392698a1a4ba952c70b` — matching `verified_at_sha` in the attestation. But the `stale-head` error reports the "current HEAD" as `f1dd41a8f09967dd60c7aefb5e43c6f62fa119af`, a commit titled "Diagnose MCP client PAT wiring in doctor" that:

- exists as a git object (`git cat-file -t f1dd41a8... ` → `commit`) — so it is reachable in the shared object store — but
- is not the tip of `origin/main`, `gerrit/main`, nor the reviewing worktree's own branch/HEAD (`compliant-lemon-grunion-impl`, confirmed at `9a94ef9737fb` throughout, via `git reflog`).

This value was **identical across two independent `review-plan` invocations ~15 minutes apart** (different `signed_at` timestamps, same reported "HEAD"), which rules out an ordinary live race (a live race would show a *different*, more-recent HEAD each retry as `main` continued to move) and instead points at a **stuck/foreign value being read**, not a genuinely fresh git query against the reviewing worktree.

`attest.py`'s `stale-head` path calls `signing.head_sha(_config.repo_root(repo_root))`, where `head_sha` (`src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py:202`) runs `git -C <repo_root> rev-parse HEAD`. `_config.repo_root(None)` resolves, in order, `explicit arg > REBAR_ROOT env > git toplevel of cwd` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:74`). `REBAR_ROOT` was confirmed unset in the reviewing shell and in `~/.zshrc`/`~/.zprofile`/`~/.bashrc`/`~/.bash_profile`. The reviewing worktree's own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` should return its own linked-worktree root, so `repo_root` should resolve correctly to the reviewing worktree — yet the returned HEAD belongs to neither that worktree nor either remote's main.

Working hypothesis (unconfirmed — needs a maintainer with instrumentation access): the attested-mode review path may use an internal temporary checkout/worktree to pin `ref=origin/main` for the review, and that temp path may not be uniquely namespaced per invocation. On a host running ~90 concurrent agent worktrees (confirmed via `git worktree list` at the time of this report) each independently running `rebar review-plan`, two concurrent invocations could collide on a shared temp-checkout path, leaving one invocation's HEAD-freshness check reading another invocation's (or another ticket's) checked-out commit.

## Impact

An epic-level (or any ticket with no scoped `file_impact`) plan-review can PASS its content review yet permanently fail to sign under concurrent multi-agent load, because the currency check races against unrelated concurrent reviews rather than the reviewing worktree's own state. This blocks `claim` (directly, and via the parent-claim cascade for every child ticket) with no available remediation path other than the disallowed `--force`.

## Reproduction

1. On a host running many concurrent `git worktree`-based rebar checkouts, each with active agent sessions.
2. From one worktree, run `rebar review-plan <epic-id>` on an epic with no `file_impact` (forces the unscoped/fail-safe currency path).
3. Review computes and signs a PASS, but the sign step's freshness check reports a `stale-head` error whose "current HEAD" does not match `git rev-parse HEAD` in the reviewing worktree, nor `origin/main`, nor `gerrit/main`.
4. Retry immediately: the SAME foreign HEAD value is reported again (not a newer one), indicating a stuck/foreign read rather than a live race against `main` continuing to move.

## Scope (proposed, needs confirmation by whoever picks this up)

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` (the `stale-head` currency check, `CURRENCY_BASIS_FAIL_SAFE` path)
- Whatever attested-mode temp-checkout mechanism backs `source=attested` review (not yet located in this investigation — needs tracing from the review entry point through to wherever an attested snapshot's local checkout path is constructed)
- `src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py::head_sha` (confirm whether `repo_root` passed to it is ever something other than the reviewing worktree's cwd-derived root)

## Non-goals

Fixing the underlying "unscoped whole-HEAD invalidation is a blunt/racy proxy" design tension (that's a legitimate design choice per `drift_floor.py`'s own docs) — this bug is specifically about the HEAD VALUE READ being wrong/foreign, not about whether whole-HEAD invalidation is the right granularity.
compiled_state.title: Unscoped plan-review "fail-safe" HEAD check resolves to a foreign, unrelated commit under concurrent multi-worktree review
